entries.title: Job 12:2
segments: Ye; Zophar and his friends; spoken in irony, meaning that they made vain pretentions.

entries.title: Job 12:4
segments: Who calleth--he answereth; or, who called--he answered.  I, who have been accustomed to call upon God, and receive answers from him, am now laughed to scorn.

entries.title: Job 12:5
segments:
Ready to slip; when a man falls into trouble, he is overlooked or treated with contempt by those who are in prosperity. 
 
  A lamp despised; a torch that is burned out, and therefore thrown away, as no longer of any service to the bearer. 
 
Men who are greatly courted and whose influence is eagerly sought in prosperity, are often overlooked and despised in adversity, and treated as if they were of no worth.

entries.title: Job 12:6
segments:
The tabernacles of robbers; very bad man are often prospered in this world, while very good men are afflicted. 
 
Though God is acquainted with all the wickedness of the wicked, and they are entirely dependent on him, yet in this world he often suffers them to prosper, and pours upon them abundance of earthly blessings.

entries.title: Job 12:9
segments:
In all these; in the proofs which all these classes of animals give of God's universal power and providence. 
 
  Hath wrought this; the whole course of nature and providence, in which is included the prosperity of the tabernacles of robbers,

entries.title: Job 12:11
segments: The ear try words?--the mouth taste his meat? there is here an implied comparison: as the mouth can distinguish between savory and unsavory food, so the ear of a wise man can discern between wise and foolish words.

entries.title: Job 12:12
segments: With the ancient; with aged men, to whose wisdom I have access as well as you.

entries.title: Job 12:16
segments: Are his; they are under his control, and all their circumstances directed by him.

entries.title: Job 12:18
segments:
Looseth the bond of kings; that is, according to our version, their authority over their subjects. 
 
  Girdeth their loins with a girdle; strengtheneth them for governing.  But many prefer to render, "He bindeth a band upon their loins."  The whole verse will then mean that he sets kings free from their bonds, and binds them at pleasure.

entries.title: Job 12:20
segments: The most wise and trustworthy of men, when left of God, wander in darkness; their wisdom is seen to be folly, and their plans come to naught.

entries.title: Job 12:22
segments: He discovereth deep things out of darkness; his infinite knowledge of all hidden things is here considered as enabling him to control the destinies of men.

entries.title: Job 12:24
segments: Taketh away the heart; leaves them to be infatuated, and to act without wisdom or discretion.
